column2: She always welcomed warmly the people who came to her for help.
She believed it was the one thing she could do...
Fein Lu Lugus: putting an end to his wandering, he set about rebuilding the mages' Guild.

On his journey he had learned that sins can only be atoned for by moving toward the future. Mistakes and sins, what was right and what was wrong: that is not in the past, but for the world ahead to decide.
Through his efforts the Guild slowly regained its old form. And he gave the teachings he had inherited from his master, and his own experience, to many young mages, and guided them.
Some years passed, and the mages of the restored Guild wished to welcome Fein as their new head.
But he firmly declined and set out on a journey again, to search for something: not the past, but the future.
No one knows where he finally came to rest in his old age. But the seeds he left for the future have surely grown into a great tree that shelters the world.
Fein seems to have begun looking toward the future, while keeping the wounds of his past hidden in his heart.
Through the journey to save the world, he must have realised anew not only what he needs, but also those who need him.
Now he seems to be trying to grasp something new, overcoming the grief of losing so many comrades and guiding young mages toward rebuilding the Guild. Someday his wounds will surely heal...
Not by forgetting, but by keeping what was precious deep in his heart...
A sense of guilt that would never heal, a world he could only dimly feel. For a long time these tormented Fein Lu Lugus.
But time passed, and little by little he found himself again. He never gave up searching for something in the future.
And, like his master, he resolved to entrust all his experience to young mages. Having guided many mages and become a great sorcerer, in his old age he returned to the tower,
the tower that held his warm memories...
Leyla Vigrid: caught up in the chaos as a knight of the Empire, she resolved to return to her own country.
The Empire was in utter chaos, but she worked to rebuild the nation together with people who shared her convictions.
She had not forgotten the Empire's crimes, but she felt her mission was to protect the ordinary people who lived there.
It took a long time for the country to find its calm again, but she never gave up and saw it through.
The knights were re-formed with her at their head, and she worked there for her country all her life.
To protect the future, to fight for what she believed in, and never to bow to any injustice: she passed those ideals on to the young knights.
